transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I feel like I’m constantly revved up at work, taking on too many projects at once and I can’t slow my mind or my pace down. It has gotten to the point where it's hard to focus on my normal tasks, so my employer suggested I come in for an evaluation.
Do you experience excessive worry or fear about everyday things, even when there's no apparent reason to be worried?

No, I wouldn't really say I feel worried or afraid of everyday things. It's more that my mind is constantly racing with excitement and all these big plans I have for work, so I just feel incredibly sped up rather than anxious.
Do you often act on impulse, such as interrupting others, blurting out answers, or engaging in impulsive behaviors, without fully thinking them through?

Yes, I've definitely been acting on impulse a lot lately. I've put a bunch of expensive software and business books on my credit card, driven way too fast at night because I felt invincible, and even sent some flirty messages to clients. In the moment, it all just felt like it was part of this big, exciting plan, even though I know it could get me in trouble.
Have you experienced a persistent elevated, expansive, or irritable mood for a significant period, or has this feeling of being 'revved up' been more episodic, coming and going over time?

This revved-up state has been persistent for most of the time since I started my full-time job, though there have been a few shorter periods where I felt flat and unmotivated. Within this state, my mood swings wildly—I can feel on top of the world one minute, and then get extremely snappy and irritated at my mom or coworkers the next.
Can you tell me more about these periods where you felt flat and unmotivated, how long they lasted, and what triggered the shift back to feeling revved up?

Those flat periods lasted about a couple of weeks where my energy completely crashed, and I'd just sit at home staring at my laptop and ignoring my friends. Even during those low-energy times, I still heard that man's voice and believed the spreadsheets were secret tests. I'm really not sure what triggered the shift back to feeling revved up; it just seemed to happen on its own.
Can you tell me more about the man's voice you heard and the belief that spreadsheets were secret tests, like what that voice said and when you started experiencing these things?

The voice is a man's voice that comments on what I'm doing, saying things like "You're messing that up" or "They're watching you," especially when I'm alone late at the office or trying to sleep. I also believe the partners are secretly testing me with weird emails and hidden messages in spreadsheets because they know I'm smarter than the others. These things started a couple of months after I began my full-time job and have been happening for most of this past year.
Have you ever questioned the reality of the voice you hear or the secret tests you believe are being conducted, or do you firmly believe they are real?

I firmly believe they are completely real. Even though my coworkers and parents tell me it's just normal work and that there's nobody actually there, the voice and the secret tests in the spreadsheets feel totally genuine to me.

Can you describe in more detail what you mean by 'the voice' and how it relates to your work and the secret tests, and do you think this voice is coming from inside your mind or from an external source?

The voice definitely sounds like a distinct man speaking from outside my head, even though nobody is actually there. It connects directly to the secret tests because the voice and the feeling of being tested happen at the same time, especially when I'm highly energetic and racing through work projects.
Have you experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, in addition to hearing the man's voice?
No, I don't see things that aren't there. It is strictly just that male voice I hear, especially when I'm working late alone or trying to fall asleep.
Do you believe the voice you hear and the secret tests are connected to a larger plot or conspiracy involving you, or are they isolated events?

They definitely feel connected, almost like a specific plan for me. When the voice says "They're watching you," I know it means the partners at my firm, who I believe picked me out because I'm smarter than the others. I'm convinced they are secretly testing me through those weird emails and hidden messages in the spreadsheets.
Can you tell me if you've ever had a period where you didn't believe in the secret tests or hear the man's voice, and if so, what was different about that time compared to now?

Yes, before I started this full-time job and during the first month or two of it, I never heard the voice or thought about any secret tests. Back then, my life was much more balanced with part-time work, community college classes, hiking, and hanging out with my friends. Now, I'm just completely consumed by work stress, overtime, and constantly feeling sped up.

Can you describe how your thoughts are organized when you're hearing the voice or thinking about the secret tests, and do you feel like your thoughts are racing or disconnected from each other during those times?

Yes, when I hear the voice and think about the secret tests, my thoughts race incredibly fast at the exact same time. My mind jumps rapidly from the new tax workflow, to starting my own firm, to how the IRS is outdated, which makes it hard to explain things to others without rambling and causing confusion.

Can you tell me more about how your thoughts seem to connect the voice, the secret tests, and your work projects, and do you feel like there's a logical flow to these connections or if they seem disjointed?

To me, it feels like a big, exciting, connected plan where staying up late racing through projects, hearing that voice comment on me, and finding secret tests in the spreadsheets all fit together. But because my thoughts are jumping so fast from one idea to another, other people find my explanations disjointed and really hard to follow.

Can you describe if there are times when the voice or the belief in secret tests seems to fade into the background or becomes less prominent when you're in a highly energetic and productive state, or if these elements remain constant?

No, they don't fade into the background at all; they actually happen at the exact same time. When I'm staying up late, feeling totally wired and racing through work projects, I still hear that voice commenting on me and remain convinced the partners are secretly testing me through the spreadsheets.
Do you think the voice you hear and the secret tests you believe in are part of your own thoughts and feelings, or do you think they are being imposed on you by some external force or entity?

I'm certain they are coming from the outside, not my own thoughts. The male voice sounds like an actual person commenting on my actions from the outside, and I believe the partners at the firm are the ones orchestrating the secret tests in my spreadsheets. It feels like they are deliberately doing this to me, rather than it being something from inside my own mind.
Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where you didn't believe in the secret tests or heard the man's voice, and what triggered the return of these beliefs and experiences?
Since those experiences started a few months into my job, they haven't really gone away or stopped. Because of that, I haven't had a period where they completely disappeared and then returned.

Can you tell me if you have ever experienced a period where your thoughts, the voice, and the belief in secret tests all stopped for a significant amount of time, and if so, what was happening in your life during that time?

No, those experiences haven't stopped for any significant period since they first started about ten months ago. Even during those couple of weeks when my energy completely crashed and I felt flat, the voice and the belief in the secret tests stayed just as constant. They have pretty much been with me the entire time I've had this full-time job.
Can you describe how the voice and secret tests affect your daily life and relationships, and do you feel like they are influencing your decisions or behaviors in any significant way?

They’ve completely disrupted my life because I spend hours obsessing over spreadsheets looking for hidden messages, which has led to missed deadlines and a formal performance review. Also, hearing the voice constantly comment on my mistakes makes me so anxious that I've completely isolated myself from my friends and family because I'm just too consumed by these tests to socialize.

Can you tell me if you've ever had a period where you felt extremely happy, irritable, or had an exaggerated sense of your own importance, and if so, did the voice and the belief in secret tests seem to intensify during those times?

Yes, absolutely. When I am in those highly energetic, sped-up, or irritable states, the voice and the belief about the secret tests definitely intensify and happen at the exact same time. It's like everything gets dialed up all at once when my mood is that high.
Have you ever experienced any other types of delusions, such as delusions of grandeur or persecution, in addition to believing in the secret tests and hearing the voice?

Well, I don't think it's a delusion, but I know for a fact that the partners singled me out because they realized I'm much smarter than the other clerks. They are testing me specifically because they know I have the talent to run my own firm eventually, even if my coworkers don't want to admit it.
Can you describe if the voice you hear and the beliefs about secret tests ever seem to be directly related to your own thoughts or feelings, or if they always appear to come from an external source?

They always feel completely external and never like they are my own thoughts or feelings. The voice is a distinct male voice commenting on my actions from the outside, and I truly believe the partners at the firm are the ones orchestrating those secret tests in the spreadsheets.

Can you clarify if the periods where you felt extremely happy, irritable, or had an exaggerated sense of importance were distinct episodes that lasted for days or weeks at a time, or if they were more fleeting and intertwined with your other experiences?

They definitely aren't fleeting; those high-energy, irritable periods are prolonged states that last for weeks or even months at a time, making up the majority of the time since I started this job. While they usually overlap with the voice and the tests, I did have a couple of weeks where my energy completely crashed and I felt flat, but the voice and beliefs still persisted. It's really been an ongoing, major part of my life lately.
Do you think that the voice you hear and the secret tests you believe in could be related to your own thoughts and feelings, or do you still believe they are coming from an external source?

Even though my family and coworkers tell me it’s just regular work or all in my head, I still firmly believe it is coming from an external source. The voice sounds completely real and outside of me, and I know the partners are truly testing me through those spreadsheets. It all just feels far too genuine to be my own thoughts.
Can you tell me if you have ever experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as smelling or tasting things that aren't there, in addition to hearing the man's voice?
No, I have never experienced other types of hallucinations, like smelling or tasting things that aren't there. It has always just been that male voice that I hear.
Can you describe if there are times when the voice you hear or the secret tests you believe in seem to be triggered by specific events, people, or situations, or if they seem to occur randomly?

They do seem to follow a pattern rather than being completely random. The voice is most common when I'm alone late at night in the office or trying to fall asleep. Both the voice and the secret tests in the spreadsheets feel the most intense when I'm staying up late, racing through my work projects, and feeling highly energized.

Can you describe how you differentiate between the voice you hear and your own internal thoughts, and do you ever feel like the voice is influencing your actions or decisions in a way that's beyond your control?

The voice is very distinct from my own thoughts because it sounds like a real, external man speaking out loud to me, commenting on my actions by saying things like "You're messing that up" or "They're watching you." While it doesn't physically force me to do things or control my body, hearing it makes me feel incredibly anxious, distracted, and paranoid about being watched.
Do you think the voice and the secret tests could be part of an illness or a condition that's affecting your mind, rather than an actual external force or plot?

I know my parents and coworkers keep telling me it's just stress or some kind of illness, but it's really hard for me to believe that. The voice and those hidden messages in the spreadsheets feel so genuine and intentional that they just have to be real.
Have you ever experienced a period where the voice stopped or the secret tests seemed to pause, and if so, did you notice any changes in your mood, energy, or behavior during that time?

No, they actually haven't stopped or paused at all since they first started. Even during those couple of weeks when my energy completely crashed, I stopped pushing projects, and I wasn't feeling amped up anymore, I still heard the man's voice at night and remained convinced that the spreadsheets were secret tests.
Do you think it's possible that the voice you hear and the secret tests you believe in could be symptoms of an underlying mental health condition, rather than an actual external reality?

While everyone tells me there's no one there and it's just normal work, the voice and the tests still feel completely real to me. But because my life and my job have gotten so chaotic and out of control lately, I am feeling really confused and am open to this evaluation to figure out what might be going on.
Can you describe how your belief in the secret tests and the voice you hear relates to your periods of high energy and irritability, and do you think these experiences are connected or separate?

They often happen at the same time, because when I'm feeling wired, staying up late, and racing through projects, the voice comments on my actions and I feel convinced the partners are secretly testing me. However, they aren't completely tied together, because even during those couple of weeks when my energy crashed and I wasn't feeling amped up, I still heard the voice and believed the spreadsheets contained secret tests. So while they definitely intensify together, they can also happen when I'm not in that high-energy state.
